thread.title: Scientists Rebuke Potential Rollback of Climate Change Health Finding

author: world today news
title: Scientists Rebuke Potential Rollback of Climate Change Health Finding
text:
• The Trump administration is considering reversing the EPA's 2009 finding that climate change poses a danger to human health.
• Eleven scientists specializing in health and climate have expressed concerns about the potential rollback.
• The 2009 EPA decision established that greenhouse gases endanger public health and welfare.
• The original finding has been the basis for regulating emissions of carbon dioxide and methane.
• Dr. Howard Frumkin emphasized that CO2 pollution is linked to heat waves, storms, and other health issues.
• A 2019 review in the journal Science reaffirmed and expanded upon the 2009 findings, indicating increased scientific confidence in the harms of climate change.
• The 2019 review added new categories of harm, including national security, economic well-being, violence, and ocean acidification.
• Chris Field from Stanford University stated that the evidence for the endangerment finding is much stronger now than in 2009.
• Dr. Courtney Howard outlined various health threats from climate change, including heat-related illnesses and food shortages.
• Kristie Ebi noted that elevated CO2 levels reduce the nutritional content of crops, affecting 85% of all plants.
• Michael Oppenheimer suggested that the administration may attempt to circumvent scientific consensus through legal means.
• Dr. Anya Sharma highlighted the significance of the 2009 finding in establishing the health risks associated with greenhouse gas emissions.
• Ignoring the scientific consensus could exacerbate health disparities and lead to increased mortality rates and healthcare costs.
